title: Startup error
author: GOC-BC
summary: The public thread currently mixes a generic startup-error report with a later PowerToys does not start automatically follow-up, while the attached Run log mainly shows handled launcher exceptions and slow indexing rather than one clearly identified failing surface.

judgment.rationale: Before maintainers can choose a code owner or fix path, the thread needs one narrow clarification: whether the live problem is autorun-at-sign-in, a later PowerToys Run startup dialog, or both.
evidence: The original issue body says only Startup error with no visible expected behavior or quoted error text, but it includes a bug-report ZIP and a text attachment.
A later commenter says PowerToys also does not automatically start on their PC even though the Task Scheduler job exists, and they attached another bug-report ZIP plus the exported autorun task.

The attached text log is a PowerToys Run log that shows handled Program-plugin exceptions and a long startup/indexing path, but it does not by itself prove the global autorun failure described in the comment.
Current repository code creates the autorun task through src/runner/auto_start_helper.cpp, which is a different ownership path from the PowerToys Run plugin startup log included in the thread.
judgment.recommended_action: Ask the reporter to separate the exact user-visible startup symptom so maintainers know whether to investigate autorun task execution, launcher startup, or a different surface.

fix_assessment.rationale: A PowerToys fix may exist, but the current thread still bundles at least two different startup symptoms into one issue, so there is not yet a single scoped code path to propose.

issue_context.summary: The issue contains two different startup narratives: an original generic startup error with attached Run logs, and a later comment claiming PowerToys fails to auto-start even though an autorun task is present.
known_information: The original report is on Microsoft Store PowerToys 0.100.2.0 and includes a bug-report ZIP plus a text log attachment.
The follow-up comment adds a second bug-report ZIP and an exported Task Scheduler XML for the autorun job.
The shared text log shows PowerToys Run starting, handled Program-plugin exceptions, and a long Program plugin indexing cost.
No maintainer response, assignee, or linked fix attempt is visible.
inferences: The issue is currently underspecified because startup error and does not automatically start on my PC could belong to different components and ownership paths.
The available PowerToys Run log may be related to slow or noisy startup, but it does not uniquely explain why the entire app would fail to auto-launch at sign-in.
issue_context.analysis: The right next step is a specific clarification request, not a generic demand for more logs. The thread already has attachments; what is missing is a clear statement of which startup failure maintainers are meant to solve.
initial_investigation: The downloaded PowerToys Run log shows handled Program-plugin exceptions and a long startup/indexing path, including Win32 program indexing that lasts roughly a minute.

The exported autorun task is a standard PowerToys logon trigger pointing at PowerToys.exe, which suggests the reporter's follow-up comment is about sign-in launch rather than only the launcher plugin exceptions.

src/runner/auto_start_helper.cpp and src/runner/general_settings.cpp show that autorun task registration is separate from PowerToys Run plugin initialization, so the issue needs a clearer symptom split before routing.

information_gaps.information: Whether the current failure is that PowerToys never appears in the tray at sign-in, or that PowerToys launches but shows a later startup error dialog.
information_gaps.why_needed: This determines whether maintainers should investigate autorun task execution, the runner, or PowerToys Run itself.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Reply with which of those two behaviors you currently see on the affected machine, and whether they happen every sign-in or only sometimes.

information_gaps.information: A screenshot of the visible startup error dialog, or the exact error text quoted verbatim if a screenshot is not available.
information_gaps.why_needed: The specific message will identify which PowerToys component is failing, which the current generic title does not reveal.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: When the problem happens again, capture the dialog and upload the screenshot through the GitHub web UI, or paste the exact message text in a comment.

information_gaps.information: Whether manually launching PowerToys.exe works normally after the failed sign-in start, and whether the Task Scheduler job reports a visible Last Run Result when the autorun symptom occurs.
information_gaps.why_needed: This separates task did not launch from task launched but startup failed later.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: After the next failure, try launching PowerToys manually once and note whether it starts; if the issue is autorun-related, also share the Task Scheduler Last Run Result text or code for the PowerToys autorun task.

actions.label: Clarify startup symptom and attach error screenshot

comment.body:
Thanks for attaching the text log and the autorun task export. The remaining blocker is not more logs in general; it is that the public thread currently mixes at least two different startup symptoms: a generic startup error and a later report that PowerToys does not auto-start even though the Task Scheduler job exists.

**Needed**
1. Please confirm whether the current failure is **(a)** PowerToys never appears in the tray at sign-in, or **(b)** PowerToys launches and then shows a startup error dialog.
2. Please upload a screenshot of the startup error dialog through the GitHub web UI, or quote the exact message text if a screenshot is not available.
3. If the sign-in launch is the failing path, please also confirm whether manually launching PowerToys works afterward and what Task Scheduler shows as the task's Last Run Result.

That will tell us whether to inspect autorun task execution, the runner, or PowerToys Run/plugin startup.
